newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PRESS DIGEST - Israel - Thurs Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Israel - Thurs Oct 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu irked by Palestinian President Arafat's 'stalling' on Hebron.
- Hebron settlers plan 'defence force'.
- Israeli negotiators arrive in Taba for talks with Palestinian Authority.
- Settlers vow to take to streets again.
- Central Bureau of Statistics labels 1996 a year of slowing economic growth.
- Industry and Trade Minister Sharansky calls on Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel to lower interest rates.
- Hyundai to supply Bezek with $12.5 million of fiber-optic cables.
- Dotan Communications forms alliance with U.S. public relations firm Fleishman-Hillard.
HAARETZ
- Arafat blames Israel of "dictating a racist plan to divide Hebron".
- Frenkel will support taxes on savings.
- Jerusalem Mayor Olmert: municipality will continue to demolish illegal buildings in East Jerusalem.
- Hebron settlers to ministers: attacks on Jews expected after redeployment.
- Former Central Bank Governor Bruno: interest rate is inordinate; drastic budget cuts needed.
- Frenkel: yearly inflation at 11-12 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Anger in Israel: Arafat evading Hebron agreement. Foreign Minister Levy: 'he's stretching things out and trying to create a crisis.'
- Central Bureau of Statistics: Drop in growth rate to 3.8 percent; fall in tourism and export growth.
- IDF prefers to leave Hebron at night
- Defence Minister Mordechai: it seems Syria plans a military action.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu: Israel will not tolerate last minute extortion.
- Arafat rejects Israeli proposal: "we are heading for a crisis".
- Tensions ahead of French President Chirac's visit.
- Switch in Frenkel's stance: supports Brodet comission report including taxes on short-term savings.
- Hebron settlers: we'll return fire if Palestinian police fire on Jewish community in Hebron.
- Islamic groups abroad passing money to Israeli counterparts reach Hamas.
GLOBES

- Central Bureau of Statistics: sharp slowdown in economic activity, growth and exports. growth 3.8 percent against 7.1 percent in 1995; Export growth 3.7 percent against 10.9 percent in 1995; 7.5 percent expected rise in imports; personal consumption at 6.1 percent; investment in fixed assets to rise by 8 percent.
- Contacts to achieve 'integrated economic process'. DJS
